newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian central bank to stop retail services.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian central bank to stop retail services.

text.p: Nigeria's central bank will stop retail banking activities from next January, military ruler General Sani Abacha said.
He told an economic conference here the apex bank's withdrawal from retail banking was to encourage commercial banks to widen the scope of their own activities.
"With this action, government hopes to restore confidence in our banking sector and attract greater foreign participation and achieve efficiency," he said.
Abacha introduced two new laws last year to encourage foreign investment.

Nigeria's banking sector has been plagued by fraud and in 1994, the government set up failed banks tribunals to try persons believed to have contributed to the distress in about one third of the country's banks.
Dozens of culprits including bank executives have been imprisoned by the tribunals and some of the stolen funds recovered.

The Abuja conference dubbed "Economic Summit", is being attended by members of the business community and government officials and is convened to discuss ways of reforming the country's stagnant economy.
Delegates will debate macroeconomic policy, trade and investment in the long and short term before making recommendations to the government.
